title: PagerRoute
problem_statement: Mid-size engineering teams spend an average of 4-6 hours per major incident on manual triage because alerts land on a generic on-call rotation rather than the engineer who owns the affected service. Existing tools like PagerDuty require weeks of configuration and a dedicated SRE function that teams under 50 engineers cannot staff. When pages reach the wrong person, MTTR compounds as engineers wake colleagues and hunt for runbooks across Confluence and Slack. A lightweight service-ownership routing layer that auto-assigns PagerDuty and CloudWatch alerts with inline runbook links can close this gap for the long tail of SaaS engineering teams priced out of enterprise incident tooling.
target_users: On-call software engineers at mid-size SaaS companies (20-200 engineers) paged for services outside their domain
Engineering managers who define on-call schedules and need MTTR and repeat-incident visibility without a dedicated SRE
Platform or SRE engineers responsible for configuring alert routing rules and maintaining service ownership registries
Engineering directors who need incident trend data to justify reliability investments to leadership
user_stories: As an on-call software engineer, I want incoming alerts routed to me only when the triggered service is one I own so that I am not paged for incidents outside my domain
As an engineering manager, I want a tiered escalation policy (primary -> secondary -> manager) per service so that incidents are never silently dropped when the primary is unavailable
As a software engineer during an incident, I want a direct runbook link inline in the alert notification so that I can begin diagnosis without searching Confluence
As an SRE, I want to declare service ownership in a .pagerroute.yml file committed to each repo so that the ownership registry stays in sync without manual dashboard updates
As an engineering manager, I want MTTR broken down by service and on-call engineer over trailing 30 days so that I can identify reliability hotspots and coaching opportunities
As an on-call engineer, I want to acknowledge or reassign an alert from Slack with a single button click so that I do not need to open a separate dashboard during an incident
As an engineering director, I want a weekly digest of total incident count, median MTTR, and repeat-incident rate per service so that I can assess whether reliability investments are working
acceptance_criteria: When an alert fires in PagerDuty or CloudWatch, PagerRoute identifies the owning engineer from the service registry and pages them within 60 seconds; alerts with no registered owner fall through to the team-level rotation
An on-call engineer can acknowledge, reassign, or escalate an alert via Slack action button; the action is reflected in the PagerRoute dashboard within 10 seconds
Service ownership defined in .pagerroute.yml on the main branch is reflected in live routing rules within 5 minutes via webhook after a push
If the primary on-call does not acknowledge within the admin-configured timeout (5-60 minutes), PagerRoute escalates to the secondary and sends a Slack DM to the engineering manager
The MTTR dashboard shows median and p90 acknowledge-time and resolve-time per service for trailing 7, 30, and 90 day windows, refreshing every 5 minutes
PagerRoute sustains at least 500 concurrent active alerts with p99 routing latency under 10 seconds, verified in load testing before GA
A new team can complete setup (connect PagerDuty, link Slack, register one service) in under 20 minutes via the self-serve onboarding flow, validated with 5 usability test participants

success_metrics.metric: Median MTTR (alert fire to incident resolved) for workspaces active for 60+ days
success_metrics.baseline: 47 minutes — industry benchmark for mid-size SaaS teams (PagerDuty State of Incidents 2023)
success_metrics.target: Median MTTR under 28 minutes within 60 days of adoption across all active workspaces

success_metrics.metric: Alert misrouting rate (pages sent to an engineer who does not own the triggered service)
success_metrics.baseline: Estimated 35% based on pre-launch interviews with 12 teams using manual rotation tools
success_metrics.target: Below 5% misrouting rate across all active workspaces within 30 days of onboarding

success_metrics.metric: Weekly active workspaces (at least one alert acknowledged via PagerRoute in a 7-day period)
success_metrics.target: 150 active workspaces within 6 months of GA

success_metrics.metric: 30-day workspace retention (workspace routes at least one alert in week 5 after signup)
Time-to-first-alert (minutes from completing onboarding to first alert correctly routed to a registered service owner)
success_metrics.baseline: No existing benchmark; target derived from usability testing with 8 engineering managers
success_metrics.target: Median time-to-first-alert under 25 minutes for new workspaces

risks_open_questions: PagerDuty API rate limits may throttle ingestion for large workspaces with high alert volume; need burst capacity validation and exponential backoff before GA
Ownership YAML may drift from reality when teams reorganize; need staleness detection (e.g., flag services with no git activity from the listed owner in 90 days)
OpsGenie and VictorOps users represent ~30% of the TAM — is multi-provider alert ingestion required at launch or is PagerDuty-first acceptable?
GDPR: on-call schedules and response-time data are employee records; legal review required before enabling EU workspaces
Per-seat pricing may discourage adoption in large orgs; per-workspace and per-service models need validation with 15+ prospective customers before GA
Services with multiple co-owners: should PagerRoute page all owners simultaneously or require a primary/secondary designation at the service level?
Engineering managers who are non-technical may reject YAML-based ownership configuration — need usability research to determine if a GUI fallback is required at launch
out_of_scope: Building a native alerting or monitoring system; PagerRoute routes alerts from existing tools and does not replace PagerDuty or CloudWatch
Integration with OpsGenie or VictorOps in v1
Incident postmortem creation or management workflows
AI-generated incident summaries or automated root cause analysis
Native mobile app; Slack is the mobile surface for alert acknowledgment
Customer-facing status page generation or SLA tracking
On-call compensation tracking or schedule fairness analytics
